correctness.rationale: The path-weight formula is exact for positive ordered compositions; bounding intermediate harmonic factors gives a two-sided coefficient-series sandwich. The derivative identity for powers of \(-\log(1-z)\) gives the uniform \(kH_{h-1}^{k-1}/h\) coefficient bound, and truncation to \(h^{1-\varepsilon}\) yields its sharp fixed-k leading term. Because log h/log n tends to theta in (0,1), geometric-series domination proves the hitting constant and tight size-biased-geometric jump count. Restricted compositions yield uniform giant index and independent small-jump logarithmic scales, and uniform harmonic-factor ratios transfer the result. Tested exact path enumeration, rational dynamic programming, and asymptotic numerical consistency: checker.py, 497 assertions. Finite checks are not infinite proofs.

residual_risks: A broad theorem on regenerative compositions or logarithmic compositions may imply the conditioned one-giant-jump path law without using the same terminology.
The exact generating-function coefficient calculation uses established combinatorial identities; the novelty claim attaches to the conditioned harmonic descent limit, not to those identities.
Source comparison does not constitute an exhaustive search of every historical paper or prove priority.

value.rationale: The near-start clade deficit \(h=n^{\theta+o(1)}\) is the natural gap between single-jump and bulk occupation regimes in the critical beta-splitting tagged-leaf chain. The exponent-dependent hitting coefficient, size-biased-geometric conditioned number of transitions, and uniform giant-step position with independent log-uniform remaining decrements together supply a structural rare-event genealogy description not determined by the known O-bound. The object and observables arise from the model, and the claim is broader and more informative than a numerical special case.
